sections.title: Ecommerce platform SEO Algeria needs hreflang readiness
sections.body: Ask the vendor or implementation team to demonstrate separate, stable URLs for every language version the store intends to maintain. Each page should be able to declare its own language, canonical URL and reciprocal hreflang relationships without relying on client-side switching. Test products, categories, policy pages and unavailable translations, not only the home page. Confirm how the platform handles regional codes, default-language fallbacks and x-default where appropriate. Arabic support must include right-to-left layout, readable mixed-direction product names, localised navigation, form validation and administrative workflows; an Arabic font toggle alone is insufficient. Decide whether inventory and price data are shared while descriptive content remains independently editable. The store also needs a process for keeping delivery and COD terms aligned between versions. Prefer a system that makes missing or stale translations visible to editors. Hreflang is useful only when the underlying pages are accurate, indexable equivalents rather than automatically generated copies with conflicting information.

sections.title: Demand controllable structured data and page templates
sections.body: Inspect the markup produced by a real product template. The platform should let the team align product structured data with visible names, prices, currencies, availability, identifiers and genuine review information. It should not force unsupported fields or duplicate conflicting product entities when a theme and extension both emit markup. Breadcrumb data should match visible navigation, and organisation details should remain centrally maintained. Beyond schema, editors need control over page titles, descriptions, headings, image alternative text and useful category copy without editing theme code. Developers need access to templates when catalogue-wide corrections are necessary. Test variants, sale prices, out-of-stock products and products without every identifier because edge cases often expose unreliable defaults. Validation tools can confirm syntax, not truth, so compare rendered data with the page and the source catalogue. Select for controllability and consistency rather than for the number of schema types listed on a sales page.

sections.title: Test page speed after themes and commerce features
sections.body: A blank demonstration store says little about production performance. Build representative product, category, search and order pages with realistic images, variants, analytics and approved extensions. Test them on mobile connections and modest devices. Look for oversized images, layout movement, delayed interaction, excessive script execution and third-party widgets that block useful content. The platform should support responsive image output, compression, caching and predictable asset loading, but configuration and theme discipline still matter. Check whether essential product text and links appear in rendered HTML without waiting for fragile client-side requests. Compare the base system with the proposed implementation rather than attributing every result to the brand of platform. Establish a performance budget and identify who can remove or replace features when it is exceeded. Page speed is not a one-time procurement checkbox; catalogue changes, tracking additions and extension updates require recurring checks against the same representative templates.

sections.title: Model Arabic content, COD and delivery workflows
sections.body: Run the proposed operational journey from product import to order follow-up. Editors should be able to maintain Arabic and other language content without overwriting one another, preview direction and formatting, and update shared facts safely. Customers need visible, accurate information about COD eligibility, delivery coverage, charges, confirmation steps and returns before they submit an order request. The platform should support the store's real status flow without labelling an unconfirmed request as a completed sale. Test addresses, telephone formats, required fields, validation messages and keyboard use on mobile. If confirmation happens through telephone or messaging, document how consent, status and customer communication are recorded. Integrations should fail visibly and allow recovery without losing the order. Avoid choosing a system because an extension promises local support without testing its maintenance, data handling and compatibility. Operational clarity protects customers and creates cleaner measurement; SEO cannot repair contradictory fulfilment information generated by disconnected workflows.

sections.title: Check URLs, crawling and migration controls
sections.body: Create a test catalogue and inspect its URL patterns for products, categories, variants, pagination, filters, internal search and tracking parameters. The team should be able to define which pages are indexable, set appropriate canonicals, edit redirects and generate an XML sitemap containing intended canonical URLs. Navigation and breadcrumbs should expose priority pages through ordinary links. Check status-code behaviour for removed products and malformed paths rather than trusting a custom error design. Ask how releases, application updates and extension changes are tested and rolled back. For migration, require an exportable URL inventory and a maintainable redirect map; changing platforms without preserving useful destinations can disrupt discovery and customer bookmarks. Access controls should let developers, editors and external partners receive only the permissions they need. These capabilities are more valuable than an abstract SEO switch because they allow the store to diagnose, correct and verify conditions throughout the catalogue's life.

sections.title: Use an evidence-led platform comparison
sections.body: Give each shortlisted system the same scenarios and record whether the result was demonstrated, configurable, custom-built or unavailable. Include language URLs, Arabic rendering, product schema, category editing, image handling, COD communication, filtering, redirects, exports and access control. Do not turn the table into a universal score or accept paid placement as evidence of suitability. Note implementation dependencies, ongoing ownership and the consequence if a required extension stops being maintained. Ask the people who will operate the store to complete routine tasks during the trial, while a technical reviewer inspects rendered output and failure cases. Before signing, identify data export paths and the cost of reversing the decision. After implementation, run the ecommerce SEO checklist for Algeria against the production templates and verify accepted requirements. The best-supported choice is the one that satisfies documented needs with manageable complexity, not the platform with the longest generic feature list.
